acceptance_criteria.text: A new LinkedList() is empty: len() is 0, to_list() returns [], and iterating yields nothing.
insert(value) with no index appends the value at the tail; inserting 1, 2, 3 in order gives to_list() == [1, 2, 3] and len() == 3.

insert(value, index) inserts the value so it ends up at that position: index 0 inserts at the head, index == len(list) inserts at the tail, and a middle index inserts between existing nodes, preserving the order of other elements.
insert with an index that is negative or greater than len(list) raises IndexError and leaves the list unchanged; a non-integer index (e.g. 'a' or 1.5) raises TypeError.

delete(value) removes the first node equal to value and returns True; it works for head, middle, and tail nodes and for a single-element list, and len() decreases by 1; when duplicates exist only the first occurrence is removed.
delete(value) on an empty list or with a value not present returns False and leaves the list unchanged.
search(value) returns the zero-based index of the first node equal to value, or -1 if the value is not present (including on an empty list).

reverse() reverses the list in place so to_list() returns the elements in the opposite order, and returns None; it works for lists of length 0, 1, 2 and many; after reversing, insert (append), delete, and search operate correctly on the new order (tail is updated correctly).
The module provides __len__ and __iter__ (and to_list()) that always reflect the current state after any sequence of insert, delete and reverse operations.
A pytest test file exercises every public method (insert, delete, search, reverse, len, iteration, to_list) including the success, edge and error cases above, and all tests pass.

# ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"


# ===== test_linked_list.py =====
from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll


def test_imports():
    assert Node is not None and LinkedList is not None


def test_node_attributes():
    n = Node(5)
    assert n.value == 5
    assert n.next is None
    m = Node(1, n)
    assert m.next is n


def test_empty_len():
    assert len(LinkedList()) == 0


def test_empty_head_is_none():
    assert LinkedList().head is None


def test_empty_to_list():
    assert LinkedList().to_list() == []


def test_empty_iter():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert list(iter(ll)) == []
    assert list(ll) == []


def test_empty_is_falsy():
    assert not LinkedList()


def test_empty_consistent():
    assert_consistent(LinkedList())


def test_manual_nodes_non_empty():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))
    ll._size = 3
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert ll
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_iter_yields_values_not_nodes():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    assert all(not isinstance(v, Node) for v in ll)


def test_iterating_twice_gives_same_result():
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    assert list(ll) == list(ll)
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]


def test_to_list_returns_new_list_each_call():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    a = ll.to_list()
    b = ll.to_list()
    assert a == b and a is not b
    a.append(99)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]


def test_reprs():
    assert repr(LinkedList()) == "LinkedList([])"
    assert repr(make_list([1, "a"])) == "LinkedList([1, 'a'])"
    assert repr(Node(3)) == "Node(3)"


def test_falsy_values_round_trip_and_list_truthy():
    for v in (0, None, "", False):
        ll = make_list([v])
        assert len(ll) == 1
        assert ll
        assert ll.to_list() == [v]
    ll = make_list([None, 0, None])
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, None]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_assert_consistent_detects_mismatch():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll._size = 5
    try:
        assert_consistent(ll)
    except AssertionError:
        return
    raise RuntimeError("helper failed to detect size mismatch")

# ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int (bool is rejected too) and
        IndexError if it is outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left
        unchanged when an error is raised.
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                prev = prev.next
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

import pytest

from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll


def test_imports():
    assert Node is not None and LinkedList is not None


def test_node_attributes():
    n = Node(5)
    assert n.value == 5
    assert n.next is None
    m = Node(1, n)
    assert m.next is n


def test_empty_len():
    assert len(LinkedList()) == 0


def test_empty_head_is_none():
    assert LinkedList().head is None


def test_empty_to_list():
    assert LinkedList().to_list() == []


def test_empty_iter():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert list(iter(ll)) == []
    assert list(ll) == []


def test_empty_is_falsy():
    assert not LinkedList()


def test_empty_consistent():
    assert_consistent(LinkedList())


def test_manual_nodes_non_empty():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))
    ll._size = 3
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert ll
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_iter_yields_values_not_nodes():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    assert all(not isinstance(v, Node) for v in ll)


def test_iterating_twice_gives_same_result():
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    assert list(ll) == list(ll)
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]


def test_to_list_returns_new_list_each_call():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    a = ll.to_list()
    b = ll.to_list()
    assert a == b and a is not b
    a.append(99)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]


def test_reprs():
    assert repr(LinkedList()) == "LinkedList([])"
    assert repr(make_list([1, "a"])) == "LinkedList([1, 'a'])"
    assert repr(Node(3)) == "Node(3)"


def test_falsy_values_round_trip_and_list_truthy():
    for v in (0, None, "", False):
        ll = make_list([v])
        assert len(ll) == 1
        assert ll
        assert ll.to_list() == [v]
    ll = make_list([None, 0, None])
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, None]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_assert_consistent_detects_mismatch():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll._size = 5
    try:
        assert_consistent(ll)
    except AssertionError:
        return
    raise RuntimeError("helper failed to detect size mismatch")


# ---- insert ----

def test_append_returns_none_and_orders():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert ll.insert(1) is None
    ll.insert(2)
    ll.insert(3)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_into_empty_at_zero():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.insert("x", 0)
    assert ll.to_list() == ["x"]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_at_head():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll.insert(0, 0)
    assert ll.to_list() == [0, 1, 2]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_middle():
    ll = make_list([1, 3])
    ll.insert(2, 1)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_at_len_is_tail():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll.insert(3, 2)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    ll.insert(4)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3, 4]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_tail_then_append_keeps_chain_intact():
    ll = LinkedList()
    for i in range(5):
        ll.insert(i, len(ll))
    ll.insert(99, 2)
    assert ll.to_list() == [0, 1, 99, 2, 3, 4]
    assert_consistent(ll)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [-1, -100, 4, 10])
def test_out_of_range_index_raises_and_leaves_list_unchanged(bad):
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    with pytest.raises(IndexError):
        ll.insert(9, bad)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_out_of_range_on_empty_list():
    ll = LinkedList()
    for bad in (1, -1):
        with pytest.raises(IndexError):
            ll.insert(1, bad)
    assert ll.to_list() == []
    assert ll.head is None
    assert_consistent(ll)

def test_non_integer_index_raises_type_error(bad):
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        ll.insert(9, bad)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]
    assert_consistent(ll)

    ll = LinkedList()
    obj = object()
    for v in (None, 0, "", obj, [1]):
        ll.insert(v)
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, "", obj, [1]]
    assert len(ll) == 5
    assert_consistent(ll)

# ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

import pytest

    Call after every mutation in tests.

        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count

    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll

# ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node whose value == ``value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). Values are
        compared with ``==`` (``node.value == value``); the list is not modified.
        """
        index = 0
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            if node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
            index += 1
        return -1

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node whose value == ``value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). Values are
        compared with ``==`` (``node.value == value``); the list is not modified.
        """
        index = 0
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            if node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
            index += 1
        return -1

def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

# ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node matching ``value``.

        A node matches if ``node.value is value`` or ``node.value == value``
        (identity first, like ``list.index``), so a NaN object stored in the
        list is found when searched for by that same object, while a different
        NaN object is not. The comparison is evaluated as
        ``node.value == value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). The list is
        never modified. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate to the caller.

        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` (the ``_size`` invariant) as well
        as by the end of the chain, so an accidental cycle created by editing
        ``next`` directly cannot make ``search`` loop forever.
        """
        node = self.head
        for index in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
        return -1

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll

"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node matching ``value``.

        A node matches if ``node.value is value`` or ``node.value == value``
        (identity first, like ``list.index``), so a NaN object stored in the
        list is found when searched for by that same object, while a different
        NaN object is not. The comparison is evaluated as
        ``node.value == value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). The list is
        never modified. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate to the caller.

        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` (the ``_size`` invariant) as well
        as by the end of the chain, so an accidental cycle created by editing
        ``next`` directly cannot make ``search`` loop forever.
        """
        node = self.head
        for index in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
        return -1
